answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks over the attestation graph: each step can wander only along verified edges, while stake caps prevent repeated identities from multiplying influence. A sybil cluster may build an internal trellis, but its sparse external cut has low conductance, limiting trust flow across the boundary within the walk horizon. Under bounded per-node weight, min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, even when its local atlas of endorsements appears dense.
